Singapore Tightens Rules on Digital Payment Scams After Record Losses

The Monetary Authority of Singapore reported that victims lost S$1.1 billion to scams in 2024, according to figures released in February 2025. Police recorded 51,501 scam cases last year, up from 46,563 cases in 2023. Investment scams accounted for S$320.7 million of that total, the largest share of any single category. Under the Shared Responsibility Framework, banks and telcos that fail to meet their anti-scam duties are required to reimburse affected customers. The framework took effect on 16 December 2024, following a public consultation that drew 93 written responses. A spokesperson for the Association of Banks in Singapore said member banks blocked more than 20,000 suspicious transactions during the first quarter of 2025. Officers from the Anti-Scam Command recovered S$182 million in 2024, according to figures published by the Singapore Police Force. The Cyber Security Agency of Singapore separately reported 132 ransomware cases in 2024, a 12 per cent decrease from the previous year.
